description:
FILED s427 (Opus), from the #415 `<~>` probe table.  PRE-EXISTING: verified
byte-identical on a 753ecab worktree, so it is not caused by that session's
readline/glob rule change or its tilde expansion.

perl's glob (bsd_glob, GLOB_NOMAGIC-ish behaviour) returns the pattern itself
when the pattern contains no wildcard, whether or not anything matches:

    perl                                   PCL
    glob("/etc/passwd")  -> /etc/passwd    /etc/passwd     (agrees: it exists)
    glob("/nope-xyz")    -> /nope-xyz      (empty)         <-- diverges
    glob("/home/")       -> /home/         (empty)         <-- diverges
    glob("x~y")          -> x~y            (empty)         <-- diverges
    glob("~/")           -> /home/bernt/   (empty)         <-- diverges
    glob("~nosuchuser")  -> ~nosuchuser    (empty)         <-- diverges

PCL's p-glob--expand always goes through the filesystem, so a pattern with no
wildcard that names nothing (or names a directory with a trailing slash, where
the "file" component is empty) yields nothing.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, p-glob--expand / %p-glob--expand-dir /
%p-glob--expand-pathname.  SHAPE: when the (tilde-expanded) pattern holds none
of `* ? [ {`, return a one-element vector of the pattern itself — that is
perl's rule and it makes the trailing-slash and unknown-user cases fall out.
Check `glob("{a,b}")` and the csh-style brace expansion before writing the
predicate.

BAR: cl/** change -> the full sweep is NOT optional.  Rows in
Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t (row 5 already compares glob("~"), glob("~/.bashrc")
and glob("~root") against the perl oracle) should be extended with the
non-wildcard cases when this closes.


=== s438i (Opus 5, 2026-08-23) DONE, in the shape this task specified, plus the
word model that shape needs to be correct.

perl returns a pattern holding no glob METACHARACTER as ITSELF, whether or not
anything of that name exists.  `p-glob--expand` went to the filesystem
unconditionally, so `/nope-xyz`, `/home/`, `x~y`, `~/` and `~nosuchuser` all
answered EMPTY.  `%p-glob--expand-one` now returns the tilde-expanded pattern
when it holds none of `* ? [ {` -- placed AFTER the tilde pass, which is what
makes the trailing-slash and unknown-user cases fall out for free.

THE WORD MODEL CAME WITH IT, because the literal rule is a per-WORD rule:
perl's glob takes a WHITESPACE-SEPARATED LIST of patterns (`glob("a b")` is two
results; `glob("/etc/pass* /nope-q")` is three -- probed), and bsd_glob is
invoked once per word.  `%p-glob--split-words` does that; an empty or all-blank
pattern has no words and yields nothing, as perl does.  Without it the literal
rule would have answered the single string "a b".

`{` COUNTS AS A METACHARACTER even though PCL has no brace expansion (#488):
counting it keeps `glob("{a,b}")` out of the literal rule, where it would
answer `{a,b}` -- further from perl's `a`, `b` than the empty result it gives
now.  Every other row of this task's probe table now matches perl.

TWO PRE-EXISTING GAPS SURFACED, both filed, and they are the reason t/op/glob.t
moves 14/4 -> 13/5: row 18 compares `$output1 eq $output2` from two separate
`eval q{ glob(q(./"TEST")) }` call sites and was PASSING ON NOTHING (both undef,
because that pattern has no wildcard and matched nothing).  With the values
real it fails honestly, on #489 (the scalar-context iterator is keyed by
PATTERN, not by CALL SITE, so the second call answers undef) and #490 (glob
does not strip csh quotes, so the value is `./"TEST"` where perl gives
`./TEST`).  Snapshot row edited by hand with that cause; measured alone and in
the parallel pass, both 13/5.

ONE Pl/t EXPECTATION REWRITTEN, under the s377 four-conjunct rule:
`Pl/t/glob-01.t`'s "glob with nonexistent literal file returns empty" asserted
`count:0`, which is the one answer perl never gives (probed:
`</tmp/nonexistent-xyz.txt>` is 1 element, the pattern).  It now asserts the
count AND the value -- strictly more than before -- with the probe recorded in
the comment.

MEASURED: full sweep TOTAL 18312 (+0), 0 new / 0 fixed, drops 5 = census, GATE
clean (a `cl/` change is invisible to corpus-diff, so the sweep is the gate);
companion io/ + op/ dirs, the only movers io/pvbm.t (23/5 alone, the SEVENTH
time, not edited) and op/glob.t (above); gate 166/5779, only the 13 pclxs xs
rows.  Guard: two rows in Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t (19 -> 21) -- one positive
over the five diverging shapes plus word splitting, one INVERSE that a real
wildcard still reaches the filesystem and a blank pattern has no words.
title: glob(PATTERN) with no wildcard returns EMPTY where perl returns the pattern itself
